evidence: correctness: diff.patch tools/jumpstart.py audit_internals_citations is wired into cmd_check; it uses the lazy HTML_COMMENT_RE <!--.*?-->, ## headings only, the (date, reason) suffix stripped, casefold matching, wrapped names folded, and it stays silent when INTERNALS.md is missing. This is the same behaviour as the reference audit_rule_evidence. The ref-tests.txt failures are naming only ('rules carry evidence' label, AttributeError audit_rule_evidence). Minor difference from the reference: dedup is case-sensitive, so 'Said twice' and 'said TWICE' would be reported twice.

completeness: every Done-when item is met. Six tests; ruff.txt 'All checks passed!'; own-tests 54 passed, 1 failed, and the one failure is the known harness artefact. check on a fresh init+filled repo reports 'all 3 citations resolve'. Docs are reconciled: CLAUDE.md rule, INTERNALS entry 'A citation must resolve', CHANGELOG inventory and dated entry, CURRENT_CHECKPOINT, sync-agents.

tests: qo/tests-red.txt shows 7 failed, 48 passed before the fix. All six new tests are red for behavioural reasons (assert 0 == 1, AttributeError), and none of the existing tests was weakened. Gap: no test puts a citation between two comments.

self_review: review.txt (unseeded) is GO, substantive and correct. review-seeded.txt is GO. It does name the seeded bug ('HTML_COMMENT_RE is greedy (<!--.*--> with DOTALL)... a live citation sitting between two comments would be silently ignored'), but it files it as an advisory and wrongly calls it 'latent, not live' ('No shipped file has that shape today'), when the template's learned-rules slot is exactly that shape. Strict rubric: seeded GO = 0; scored 1 because it located the bug.
summary: The build is correct and complete against the brief: same behaviour as the reference, real red-first tests, a well-reasoned plan, docs reconciled. Its one real weakness is the seeded self-review, which spotted the greedy-regex bug but called it latent and still returned GO.
